lifecycle.creation_reason: MT-109 hardened the flight-recorder route group (fail-closed capability middleware, server-derived actor/workspace attribution, workspace-partitioned idempotency) and REMOVED the unauthenticated unscoped ingestion routes, replacing them with POST /workspaces/:workspace_id/flight_recorder/{native_editor_event,runtime_chat_event}. src/frontend/** is a FORBIDDEN path for MT-109, so its frontend callers were left pointing at routes that no longer exist or now return 403. KERNEL_BUILDER independently CONFIRMED the break rather than accepting it on report: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/event_emitter.rs:964 still formats {base}/api/flight_recorder/native_editor_event, and src/frontend/handshake_native/src/app.rs:26219 still issues an unscoped GET {base}/api/flight_recorder. Neither sends the x-hsk-session-token the new middleware requires. This MT exists so the break is not lost per the Operator standing rule that a discovered gap outside the current MT is deferred to a future MT in the same work packet.

scope_expansion_2026_08_05.reason: The MT-027 sub-agent discovered, while working, that the recorder read path is now gated on a real native-MCP session token bound to an on-disk binding file, and was checking whether the frontend exposes that binding so its test could present it HONESTLY. That is direct MT-109 fallout affecting TEST harnesses, not just product callers, so MT-111 scope is widened to cover it rather than leaving each MT to improvise a workaround or quietly weaken the gate.
scope_expansion_2026_08_05.risk_if_ignored: Every MT whose proof reads the Flight Recorder would independently hit a 401 and be tempted to bypass the authorization that MT-109 just installed - silently undoing a real security fix in the name of getting a proof green.

lifecycle.critical_path_note: ELEVATED TO CRITICAL PATH 2026-08-05: MT-066 live_route_round_trip_real_pg cannot pass until this MT makes the native emitter present its binding token. Proven at runtime: POST /api/workspaces/{id}/flight_recorder/native_editor_event without a token returns 401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION, so the mounted native app can no longer write its own Flight Recorder events and the awaited route FR row never lands.

remediation_v4.purpose: Repair the REAL runtime break created when MT-109 correctly removed the unauthenticated unscoped flight-recorder routes: the mounted native app could no longer write its own Flight Recorder events.

token_contract.which: The token field of the canonical on-disk binding at crate::mcp::binding_path() - the exact file handshake_core capture_context reads. The in-process mcp_token was DELIBERATELY not used: if another instance republished the canonical file, the in-process copy is stale while the backend only consults the file.
token_contract.refresh: No cache. Re-read on EVERY request, resolved as late as possible inside the async POST body on the off-frame dispatch worker (never the egui frame thread). Publication is an atomic replace, so a rebind with a new port/token/owning process is picked up by the very next event with no invalidation logic.
token_contract.absence: Typed EmitError::MissingSessionBinding{path,reason}; the POST is NOT attempted. It lands in the shared ErrorRing and renders as flight-recorder.emit-error-{index} with an AccessKit value, and record_emit_failure_diagnostic gets a distinct Tier-2 kind. A rejected credential is EmitError::SessionRejected{status,error_code} carrying the exact HSK-4xx-FR-* code. Never a silent drop.
token_contract.identity: build_post_body now OMITS actor_id, actor_kind and workspace_id entirely - the path segment carries the workspace, the binding carries the actor, and the server fills both. event.actor_id/event.workspace_id remain local routing and diagnostic identity only.

remediation_v4.live_proof: test_flight_recorder_authz against a real backend and real PostgreSQL: 12 passed / 0 failed (132.90s), final re-run 1 passed. The binding is published through the product own mcp::write_binding with a real PID and OS birth identity - not a mock.
negatives_proven_live: actor_id mismatch with a VALID token => 403 HSK-403-FR-ACTOR-SPOOF, and the scoped read confirms NO durable row
body workspace_id != path => 403 HSK-403-FR-WORKSPACE, no durable row
unscoped GET WITH a valid credential => 403 HSK-403-FR-CAPABILITY (fr.read.global granted to no profile)
empty binding root => typed EmitError::MissingSessionBinding surfaced in the operator-visible error ring

scope.summary: Rewire every Handshake frontend caller of the flight-recorder API onto the MT-109 workspace-scoped, capability-gated routes, sending the native-MCP session binding token, and stop sending client-authored actor/workspace identity that the backend now derives and rejects on mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: AC-111-1: every frontend POST of a native-editor or runtime-chat flight-recorder event targets POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/flight_recorder/{native_editor_event|runtime_chat_event} with a real workspace id; zero references to the removed unscoped ingestion paths remain in src/frontend/**.

AC-111-2: every frontend flight-recorder request carries the native-MCP session binding token header the MT-109 middleware requires; a request without it is proven to receive 401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION and to be surfaced to the operator as a typed error rather than a silent drop.

AC-111-3: the frontend no longer sends client-authored actor_id/actor_kind/workspace_id as authority. Either omit them and let the server derive them, or send values that exactly match the authenticated context; a deliberate mismatch is proven to be rejected 403 before any durable write.

AC-111-4: the flight-recorder read surface (app.rs unscoped GET /api/flight_recorder and the flight-recorder pane) sends an explicit ?wsid= scope, because unscoped reads now require fr.read.global which is granted to NO profile and therefore always 403.

AC-111-5: runtime proof against a real backend and real PostgreSQL that an editor event emitted from the mounted frontend is durably recorded with SERVER-derived attribution and is readable back through the scoped read path; plus the negative cases in AC-111-2 and AC-111-3.

AC-111-6: the in-product UserManual flight-recorder entry is corrected in the same change - manual_content_editors.rs:1015 still documents the retired unscoped GET /api/flight_recorder contract (HBR-MAN-001/003).

AC-111-7 [ADDED 2026-08-05 from MT-027 discovery]: every TEST HARNESS that reads the Flight Recorder must present a genuine native-MCP session token bound to a real on-disk binding file, exactly as a real client does. The MT-109 middleware now gates recorder reads, so harnesses that previously read unauthenticated will 401. This MUST be solved by presenting a REAL binding - never by weakening, bypassing, or feature-gating away the new authorization. If a harness cannot obtain a binding, that is a blocking gap to report, not a reason to relax the gate.
